title: VPC Terraform modules (alpha): kickoff, scope, module list, owners, milestones
creator: Irene Choi
description:
Context
- Redwood Private (VPC + on-prem) pilots are repeatedly blocked by inconsistent customer networking setups (subnet layout, DNS, endpoints, NAT strategy, flow logs, SG boundaries, IAM permissions).
- Goal is to publish a set of Redwood-validated Terraform modules (AWS-focused, alpha scope) that provide safe defaults and clear extension points.

What this epic delivers (alpha)
1) Opinionated Terraform modules for a standard AWS private deployment footprint:
   - VPC + subnets (public/private), routing, NAT strategy (sane defaults but configurable)
   - Security group patterns for cluster nodes, load balancers, and controlled egress
   - VPC endpoints + DNS/private DNS behavior options (ECR/S3/STS/CloudWatch Logs, etc.)
   - Logging defaults (VPC Flow Logs; CloudWatch/S3 destinations with customer-owned options)
   - IAM scaffolding for installer execution role + permission boundary pattern
   - Optional placeholders/outputs for VPN/Direct Connect integrations (no provider-specific encoding)
2) Validation + testing pipeline:
   - fmt/validate, tflint, checkov (or equivalent) gating
   - integration tests standing up ephemeral VPC environments (strategy TBD for nightly vs per-PR)
3) Release/versioning process:
   - semver + changelog discipline
   - compatibility commitments and “alpha” constraints explicitly documented
4) Field-ready artifacts:
   - reference architecture + deployment guide
   - example configurations (tfvars) for design partners
   - known limitations + support/escalation paths

Non-goals (explicit)
- Multi-cloud parity beyond stubs/roadmap notes (no GCP/Azure GA module set in alpha)
- Turnkey cluster/app install (handled by redwood-private-installer / Helm)
- Deep bespoke enterprise topology support; we will document supported extension points instead

Proposed module suite (names are working; finalize in ADR-027)
- modules/vpc: VPC, subnets, route tables, NAT strategy
- modules/endpoints: Gateway + interface endpoints, private DNS behavior, endpoint SG rules
- modules/logging: Flow Logs setup + destination options + retention defaults
- modules/security-groups: Opinionated SG patterns (nodes, LB, egress) w/ documented ports
- modules/iam-installer: Installer execution role/policy scaffolding, permission boundaries
- modules/connectivity-hooks: Outputs/placeholders for VPN/DX route propagation + TGW hooks
- examples/: minimal example + design partner examples (sanitized)

Milestones (alpha target)
- M0: Kickoff + scope lock (this ticket) (Week of 2025-06-03)
- M1: ADR-027 module boundaries + public interface v0 (2 weeks)
- M2: ADR-028 validation + integration test plan (2 weeks; in parallel)
- M3: Repo skeleton + examples directory layout (Week of 2025-06-17)
- M4: Core VPC module implemented + reviewed (Weeks of 2025-06-24 to 2025-07-05)
- M5: Endpoints module + DNS options + installer alignment notes (Weeks of 2025-07-05 to 2025-07-19)
- M6: Flow logs module + destination options + retention default decision (Weeks of 2025-07-19 to 2025-08-02)
- M7: SG patterns module + least-privilege/operability compromise documented (Weeks of 2025-07-19 to 2025-08-02)
- M8: IAM installer scaffold + permission boundary pattern (Weeks of 2025-08-02 to 2025-08-09)
- M9: CI gating (fmt/validate/tflint/checkov) + provider pinning (Weeks of 2025-08-02 to 2025-08-09)
- M10: Integration test harness (ephemeral env) + cost controls (Weeks of 2025-08-09 to 2025-08-15)
- M11: Dogfood in Redwood sandbox + punch list (Weeks of 2025-08-15 onward)
- M12: Design partner pilot(s) + alpha tag release

Alpha acceptance criteria (engineering)
- Modules have clear inputs/outputs with defaults that match the reference architecture
- CI gates passing on main; security scan results triaged and documented
- At least one ephemeral integration test path runs reliably (per-PR or nightly per ADR-028)
- README sections include: supported topologies, extension points, anti-patterns, upgrade notes
- Outputs required by redwood-private-installer preflight are exposed and documented

Key decisions to lock (needs ADR / security input)
- NAT strategy defaults: per-AZ NAT GW vs cost-optimized; how we expose override without footguns
- Private DNS defaults for interface endpoints (esp. ECR) and how to detect/validate in installer
- Logging destinations: CloudWatch vs S3 default, customer-owned buckets, retention defaults
- Permission boundary stance: required vs recommended; how to integrate with customer IAM

Risks / watchouts
- Customers with forced proxies / restricted egress will need documented extension points (do not encode corporate proxy assumptions in core modules)
- Endpoint/DNS misconfig is a top failure mode (ensure installer preflight and docs are aligned)
- Integration test cost/time: must fit within CI budget; consider nightly heavy tests
- Backward incompatible changes during alpha: require pinning guidance and upgrade playbook

Comms cadence
- Weekly 30-min sync: Infra + Private Deployments + Security (DRIs above)
- Milestone review in #eng-infra and #eng-private-deployments; security sign-off checkpoints at M5/M8/M9

Next steps (this week)

- Convert milestone plan into sub-issues (ENG-4829/4837/4844/4852/4860/4883/4895 already created)
- Confirm design partner timeline with PM-913 and pilot plan doc
updates: 2025-06-04 (Irene): Created epic from discovery notes; linked PRD + ADR drafts; set initial milestone plan and DRI map.
2025-06-11 (Victor): Confirmed baseline subnet strategy: 3 AZ recommended, private subnets for compute, public for ALB/NAT; will document 2 AZ constraints explicitly.

2025-06-12 (Marcus): IAM boundary approach should be strongly recommended by default; modules must support customer-provided boundary ARN and refuse to create overly broad policies without explicit override.
2025-06-18 (Sahana): CI gating proposal: fmt/validate/tflint per-PR; checkov per-PR with allowlist for known acceptable findings; integration tests likely nightly with manual trigger for PRs.
2025-07-02 (Irene): Added due date aligned with initial alpha release candidate; flagged integration test budget as a blocker pending sandbox account decision.
2025-07-09 (Kira): Deployment guide structure drafted; requests definitive list of required VPC endpoints + DNS behaviors to avoid docs drift.
comments: Victor Alvarez (2025-06-11): For endpoints module, we should make private DNS default ON for ECR API/DKR endpoints; S3 gateway endpoint required in fully private clusters; add explicit outputs to drive installer preflight checks (e.g., endpoint IDs + private DNS enabled flags).

Naomi Feldman (2025-06-13): Please ensure we have a clear statement of what gets logged by default (flow logs) and where data resides. Also make sure opt-outs are explicit and recorded (inputs) for audit reasons.

Sean Gallagher (2025-06-20): From SRE side, we need deterministic naming/tags across modules for inventory + drift detection. Also please add a minimal runbook section for ‘what changes are risky’ (subnet/NAT/endpoints).

Markus Klein (2025-07-02): Field request: keep the ‘minimal path’ extremely short (VPC CIDR + AZ count + allowed egress destinations). Too many knobs will kill adoption; document extension patterns instead.
